mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to decline, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer demand (GDPC1) creates optimism about future economic expansion, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 2% and GDPC1 > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative despite both proxies exceeding thresholds (out-of-sample t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply-side weakness, prompting investors to price in higher future demand to offset weak output, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or non-negative during INDPRO contraction months (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below trend suggests deflationary pressure, prompting the market to anticipate lower future inflation and a rate cut, which supports positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4%, it indicates labor market strength that typically prompts the Fed to be cautious, keeping rates steady and supporting equity valuations, which drives positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during the UNRATE < 4% window (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: A large rise in retail jobs (PAYEMS) without a corresponding increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests demand-driven hiring, boosting investor confidence and producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 5% while INDPRO growth < 0% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the interaction window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in housing starts (not in the observable list, so skip supply via available proxies) — instead, a sharp drop in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 250) creates supply-side concerns, pushing down 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 102 and CPIAUCSL < 250 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent tightening in credit conditions as measured by rising RSAFS (reserves) suggests banks are reducing lending, which increases perceived risk and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative over 12 consecutive tightening months (out-of-sample).
